questions.q: How does lift depend on airspeed?
options: Proportional to airspeed and air density
Proportional to the square of airspeed
Proportional to the cube of airspeed
It does not depend on airspeed

questions.q: Stall speed in a turn with 60° of bank compared with level flight:
A normal static margin in pitch:
options: CG exactly at the neutral point for minimum drag
CG 5–15 % MAC ahead of the neutral point
CG 50 % MAC ahead of the neutral point
questions.explain: CG 5–15% of the mean chord ahead of the neutral point.

questions.q: Dive test: after you let go of the sticks the plane keeps diving. This is:
options: A CG that is too far forward, the elevator is overloaded
An aft CG, a small margin
questions.explain: A stable plane pulls out to level by itself.

options: Only airspeed, the elevator holds altitude
The total energy of the aircraft
questions.explain: The elevator splits the energy between altitude and speed.

questions.q: AIRSPEED_MIN relative to V_s should be:
questions.explain: A margin for turns and gusts.

questions.q: Roughly where is the neutral point of a flying wing?
questions.explain: With corrections for sweep; the CG is set at 15–20%.

questions.q: Cruise speed relative to stall speed is roughly:
questions.explain: Cruise is taken with a margin of ≈ 1.4 times the stall speed.
